'''{{ill|Kumano Nyakuōji Shrine}}''' (熊野若王子神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Sakyō-ku, Kyoto|ar|ساكيو-كو|ca|Sakyō|ceb|Sakyō-ku|de|Sakyō-ku (Kyōto)|fa|ساکیو، کیوتو|fi|Sakyō-ku|fr|Sakyō-ku|id|Sakyō-ku, Kyōto|it|Sakyō-ku|ja|左京区|ko|사쿄구|my|ဆခယောရပ်ကွက်၊ ကျိုတို|nl|Sakyo-ku|ru|Сакё|tr|Sakyō|uk|Район Сакьо|ur|ساکیو-کو، کیوٹو|zh|左京區|zh_yue|左京區|qid=Q1321832|lt=Sakyō Ward}}, Kyoto City. Its former Rank was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}. It was once the guardian shrine of {{ill|Zenrin-ji|de|Zenrin-ji|ja|禅林寺|zh|禪林寺|qid=Q189807|lt=Eikan-dō Zenrin-ji}} and is situated at the southern end of {{ill|Philosopher's Walk|de|Philosophenweg (Japan)|es|El Camino del Filósofo|fr|Promenade du philosophe|he|דרך הפילוסוף|id|Jalur Filsuf|it|Sentiero del filosofo|ja|哲学の道|ko|철학의 길|my|အတွေးသမားလျှောက်လမ်း|nl|Filosofenpad (Kyoto)|vi|Con đường Triết gia|zh|哲学之道|qid=Q1510488|lt=Philosopher's Walk}}. Commonly referred to as Nyakuōji Shrine, it is one of the {{ill|Kyoto's Three Kumano Shrines|ja|京都三熊野|qid=Q140447336}}.

== History ==

In {{ill|Eiryaku|fa|ایریاکو|fr|Ère Eiryaku|ia|Eiryaku|id|Eiryaku|ja|永暦|ko|에이랴쿠|ru|Эйряку|simple|Eiryaku|sr|Еирјаку|th|เอเรียกุ|tr|Eiryaku|zh|永曆 (日本)|zh_yue|永曆 (日本)|qid=Q1193895|lt=Eiryaku}} 1 (1160), {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|2=ja|3=後白河天皇|qid=Q317984|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|2=ja|3=後白河天皇|qid=Q317984|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|qid=Q3200355}} at {{ill|Zenrin-ji|de|Zenrin-ji|ja|禅林寺|zh|禪林寺|qid=Q189807|lt=Eikan-dō Zenrin-ji}}, establishing the shrine. The shrine’s name is derived from {{ill|Nyakuichi Ōji|ja|若一王子|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11616186}}, an alternative name for {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}.

In preparation for {{ill|Kumano Three Shrines|ja|熊野詣|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10403700}}, {{ill|Yamabushi|ja|修験者|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山伏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2309838}} were said to purify themselves at this shrine before embarking on their journey.

{{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|en|Ashikaga Takauji|qid=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji}} and later, in {{ill|Kanshō|en|Kanshō|qid=Q1143928|lt=Kanshō}} 6 (1465), {{ill|Ashikaga Yoshimasa|en|Ashikaga Yoshimasa|qid=Q447034|lt=Ashikaga Yoshimasa}}, held a cherry blossom viewing party at the shrine. The shrine enjoyed patronage from the [[Ashikaga Shogunate]] and various samurai clans.

Though the shrine fell into ruin during the {{ill|Ōnin War|en|Ōnin War|qid=Q385676|lt=Ōnin War}}, it was later restored by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|af|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ar|تويوتومي هيده-يوشي|arz|تويوتومى هيده يوشى|ast|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|az|Toyotomi Hideyoşi|ban|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|be|Таётомі Хідэёсі|bg|Тойотоми Хидейоши|ca|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|cdo|Hŭng-sìng Séu-gék|ckb|تۆیۆتۆمی ھیدێیۆشی|cs|Hidejoši Tojotomi|de|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|el|Τογιοτόμι Χιντεγιόσι|eo|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|es|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|et|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|eu|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|fa|تویوتومی هیده‌یوشی|fi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|fr|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|gl|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|glk|تویوتومی هیده یوشی|hak|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|he|טויוטומי הידיושי|hr|Tojotomi Hidejoši|hu|Tojotomi Hidejosi|hy|Տոյոտոմի Հիդեյոսի|ia|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|id|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|is|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|it|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ja|豊臣秀吉|ka|ტოიოტომი ჰიდეიოსი|kk|Тоётоми Хидэёси|ko|도요토미 히데요시|kw|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|la|Taicosama|lt|Tojotomi Hidejoši|lv|Tojotomi Hidejosi|mg|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ml|തൊയൊത്തോമി ഹിദെയോഷി|ms|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|nl|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|no|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|oc|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|pl|Hideyoshi Toyotomi|pt|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ro|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ru|Тоётоми Хидэёси|sc|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|sco|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|simple|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|sk|Hidejoši Tojotomi|sl|Tojotomi Hidejoši|sq|Tojotomi Hidejoshi|sr|Тојотоми Хидејоши|sv|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|tg|Тайетоми Хидзеси|th|โทโยโตมิ ฮิเดโยชิ|tl|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|tr|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|uk|Тойотомі Хідейосі|ur|تویوتومی ہیدیئوشی|vi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|war|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|wuu|丰臣秀吉|zh|丰臣秀吉|zh_classical|豐臣秀吉|zh_min_nan|Toyotomi Hideyosi|zh_yue|豐臣秀吉|zu|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|qid=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}}.

During the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}, the shrine buildings had deteriorated and were repaired. It was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}. Previously, the main shrine consisted of four sub-shrines—{{ill|Kumano Hongū Taisha|abstract|Q705035|cs|Svatyně Kumano Hongú|de|Kumano Hongū-Taisha|es|Kumano Hongū Taisha|fa|کومانو هونگو تایشا|fr|Kumano Hongū-taisha|it|Kumano Hongū Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社|la|Kumano Hongū Taisha|nl|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ru|Кумано хонгу тайся|tr|Kumano Hongū Taisha|zh|熊野本宮大社|qid=Q705035|lt=Kumano Hongū Taisha}}, {{ill|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|en|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|qid=Q335618|lt=Kumano Hayatama Taisha}}, {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|de|Kumano Nachi-Taisha|el|Κουμάνο Νάτσι Τάισα|eu|Kumano Nachi Taisha|fa|کومانو ناچی تایشا|fr|Kumano Nachi-taisha|it|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|la|Kumano Nachi Taisha|lt|Načio maldykla|ru|Кумано нати тайся|tr|Kumano Nachi-Taisha|zh|熊野那智大社|qid=Q710359|lt=Kumano Nachi Taisha}}, and {{ill|Wakamiya|en|Wakamiya|qid=Q100249640|lt=Wakamiya}}—but in {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 54 (1979), they were consolidated into a single shrine.

The shrine is home to Kyoto Prefecture’s oldest sacred {{ill|Nageia nagi|en|Nageia nagi|qid=Q3274110|lt=Nagi tree}}, estimated to be over 400 years old.

Kyoto is home to the three Kumano Shrines: {{ill|Imakumano Shrine|ja|新熊野神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17193550}}, associated with {{ill|Kumano Hongū Taisha|abstract|Q705035|cs|Svatyně Kumano Hongú|de|Kumano Hongū-Taisha|es|Kumano Hongū Taisha|fa|کومانو هونگو تایشا|fr|Kumano Hongū-taisha|it|Kumano Hongū Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社|la|Kumano Hongū Taisha|nl|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ru|Кумано хонгу тайся|tr|Kumano Hongū Taisha|zh|熊野本宮大社|qid=Q705035|lt=Kumano Hongū Taisha}}; {{ill|Kumano Shrine|ja|熊野神社 (京都市)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q106852642}}, associated with {{ill|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|en|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|qid=Q335618|lt=Kumano Hayatama Taisha}}; and Kumano Nyakuōji Shrine, associated with {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|de|Kumano Nachi-Taisha|el|Κουμάνο Νάτσι Τάισα|eu|Kumano Nachi Taisha|fa|کومانو ناچی تایشا|fr|Kumano Nachi-taisha|it|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社|la|Kumano Nachi Taisha|lt|Načio maldykla|ru|Кумано нати тайся|tr|Kumano Nachi-Taisha|zh|熊野那智大社|qid=Q710359|lt=Kumano Nachi Taisha}}.
